March 2026

Office for Students (OfS): non-executive board members

The Secretary of State for Education has appointed Evelyn Asante-Mensah, Kirstin Baker, Sumita Hutchison, Julia Mundy and Richard Stables to the board of the Office for Students (OfS) as non-executive board members.

Evelyn, Kirstin, Sumita, Julia and Richard have been appointed for 5 years from 1 May 2026.

Remuneration for this role is £9,180 per annum for an estimated time commitment of 20 days per year.

This appointment has been made under Schedule 1, paragraph 2(1)(d) of the Higher Education and Research Act 2017, which permits the appointment of up to 12 ordinary or non-executive OfS board members.

The register of interests of board members is published on the Office for Students website.

Evelyn has declared the following interests:

Chair, The Union (Manchester Metropolitan University Students’ Union)

Kirstin has declared the following interests:

Inquiry Chair, Competition and Markets Authority

Interim Chair, The Pensions Regulator

Co-Chair, Brighton, Hove & Sussex Sixth Form College

Julia has declared the following interests:

Independent Member, Audit and Risk Assurance Committee, UK Statistics Authority

Richard has declared the following interests:

Sumita has declared the following interests:

Governor, Bristol Grammar School

Evelyn Asante-Mensah, Kirstin Baker, Sumita Hutchison, Julia Mundy and Richard Stables have not declared any political activity.

The OfS is a non-departmental public body and the independent regulator of higher education in England.

Student Loans Company: non-executive board member

Natasha Toothill has been reappointed to serve a second term on the Student Loans Company (SLC) board. She will serve from 1 April 2026 for a period of 3 years.

Remuneration is £12,000 a year, rising to a maximum of £17,000 a year depending on participation in board sub-committees or other additional duties as agreed with the SLC Chair. The appointment will involve an estimated time commitment of 1.5 to 2 days a month.

Natasha Toothill has not declared any conflicts of interest or political activities.

The SLC is a non-profit making government-owned organisation that administers loans and grants to students in colleges and universities in the UK. It is a non-departmental public body of the Department for Education.

Office for Students: non-executive directors

The Secretary of State for Education has appointed Jane McCall, Neil Swift, Simon Wilde and Andrew Wilson to the board of the Office for Students (OfS) as non-executive directors.

Jane, Simon and Andrew have been appointed for 4 years from 1 September 2025. Neil has been appointed for 4 years from 2 November 2025.[footnote 1]

Remuneration for this role is £9,180 per annum for an estimated time commitment of 20 days per year.

This appointment is made under Schedule 1, paragraph 2(1)(d) of the Higher Education and Research Act 2017, which permits the appointment of up to 12 ordinary or non-executive OfS board members.

The OfS is a non-departmental public body. It is the independent regulator of higher education in England. It regulates in the interests of students and prospective students from all backgrounds.

May 2025

Office for Students: non-executive board member appointment

Neil Swift is appointed by exception to serve on the Office for Students (OfS) board. He will serve from 1 May 2025 for a period of 6 months. We have made this appointment to allow the OfS to remain lawfully constituted, as per the requirements in the Higher Education and Research Act 2017 schedule 1 (2)1, whilst a full public appointments process is undertaken.

Neil Swift will bring extensive public sector governance experience to the board and his background in regulation, accounting and finance will be a welcome addition.

Remuneration is £9,180 per annum for an estimated time commitment of 20 days per annum.

Neil has not declared any interests or any political activity.

The OfS is an arms-length body of DfE and the regulator of higher education in England.

Diversity data (all applicants - 281)

Of the 266 people who provided information on their gender, 41.35% are female.

Of the 264 people who provided information on their background, 29.55% are ethnic minority.

Of the 260 people who provided information on whether they had a disability, 4.21% have declared a disability.

Of the 136 people who provided information on their location, 60.31% are based outside London or South East.

We are committed to complying with data protection principles and ensuring privacy. As such, we are not disclosing the diversity data of the final appointments. ↩
